findings.evidence: The diff changes `if (typeof key === 'string' && isProtoKey(key))` to `if (isProtoKey(key))`, and src/utils/protoInjection.ts:1-5 already returns `typeof key === 'string' && (key === '__proto__' || key === 'constructor')`. findings.reason: set.ts:42-59 does check proto keys before the isImmutable branch, so `set(Map(), '__proto__', v)` returns the Map unchanged while `Map.set` (__tests__/Map.ts:598) stores the key. But the ordering was the same before the diff: the old check gave the same result for every key. This change didn't introduce the inconsistency and doesn't make it worse.
findings.claim: The proto-key guard comes before the immutable-collection branch, so functional set ignores '__proto__'/'constructor' on Maps while Map.set stores them.
findings.evidence: In `set`, `if (isProtoKey(key)) return collection;` comes before `if (isImmutable(collection)) return collection.set(key, value);`. __tests__/Map.ts:598 shows `Map(...).set('__proto__', {admin:true})` is a supported write. __tests__/functional/set.ts tests only '__proto__' on plain objects (lines 43-68). It has no 'constructor' case and no Map case.
